pairs.subject: web-scraping
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/resilience/mod.rs:187 Removals are only held back from Degraded upward, and sync_many asks for this through enforced_state, which answers Healthy while soaking (store.rs:865-868). So the first run judged Broken (total_collapse, healthy to suspect) still runs absence processing and can tombstone keys from a partial batch, which breaks the dedup rule that a suspect harvest never reconciles.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/resilience/store.rs:865 There are two accessors: state() reports and enforced_state() governs (neutral Healthy when not armed). preview.rs keeps an enumerated CONSEQUENCES inventory (line 57) with a test, and unjudged runs are counted separately and never credited with a transition (preview.rs:618). Recovery is a streak of judged clean runs through Probation (detect.rs:883).

crates/core/src/resilience/detect.rs:314 Per-field collapse is judged against the baseline, with the field named in the reason. The fetch-health gate comes first (detect.rs:294), so an outage gives Inconclusive, not collapse. A container_empty quiet listing gives ContentEmpty, not Broken.

crates/core/src/resilience/mod.rs:187 Suspect, the state a single collapsed run lands in, does not suppress removals, so a collapsed harvest can still tombstone. The standard requires no absence processing on any harvest flagged as collapsed.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard contradicts itself on the first rung. dedup-and-datasets and shape-change-detection say a harvest flagged as collapsed or suspect never reconciles and is quarantined at once. soak-mode-and-verdict-replay says the first rung (suspect) is inert, gates nothing, and that quarantine is earned through hysteresis. This code follows the soak ladder, which lets a single collapsed run tombstone. The registry should say whether per-run absence suppression on a Broken verdict sits outside the ladder, so it is not soaked and not hysteretic, or whether soak overrides it.

pairs.subject: web-scraping
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/datasets.rs:1344 detect_removed tombstones every live key missing from one snapshot at once. It does not wait for absence across N consecutive healthy harvests, so a single partial or rotated harvest is enough to remove entities.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/datasets.rs:1344 Tombstones on the first miss, not on a policy. Reconciliation is otherwise strong: New/Changed/Unchanged ChangeKind, last_seen refreshed on unchanged, and a returning key revives its tombstone (datasets.rs:989) instead of minting a duplicate. The only guards are the empty-batch check and the RemovalGuard state token (datasets.rs:716).

pairs.subject: web-scraping
pairs.evidence: crates/engine-http/src/lib.rs:405 The HTTP client sets only a User-Agent (by default an impersonated Chrome string, config.rs:1563) and never states a preferred representation. No probe for alternate representations or rel=alternate exists anywhere in the repo, so the acquire stage has silently decided that markup is the only answer.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine-http/src/lib.rs:405 build_client sets no Accept preference. A repo-wide grep finds Accept headers only in API apps (application/json) and the archive engine's header allowlist, with no probe step before rule authoring.
